worked_examples.problem: In-Text Question (Nutrition & Respiration): (a) What are the necessary conditions for autotrophic nutrition and what are its by-products? (b) Differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic respiration in terms of ATP yield and end-products.
worked_examples.formula: Photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 12H2O + Sunlight + Chlorophyll -> C6H12O6 + 6O2 + 6H2O. Aerobic yield = 36-38 ATP; Anaerobic yield = 2 ATP.
worked_examples.calculation:
(a) Necessary conditions: Chlorophyll pigment, solar radiation (sunlight), carbon dioxide (CO2), and water (H2O). By-products: Oxygen gas (O2) and water.
(b) Aerobic vs Anaerobic Respiration:
1. Aerobic: Occurs in mitochondria in the presence of oxygen. Glucose is completely broken down to CO2 and H2O, yielding high energy (36–38 ATP per glucose molecule).
2. Anaerobic: Occurs in cytoplasm in the absence of oxygen. In yeast (fermentation), end-products are Ethanol + CO2 + 2 ATP. In human muscle cells during strenuous exercise, end-product is Lactic Acid + 2 ATP (causing muscle fatigue and cramps).
worked_examples.finalAnswer: (a) Conditions: Sunlight, chlorophyll, CO2, H2O; by-product is O2; (b) Aerobic yields 36-38 ATP with CO2 + H2O; Anaerobic yields only 2 ATP with ethanol/lactic acid.

worked_examples.problem: In-Text Question (Transportation & Excretion): (a) What is double circulation in human beings and why is it necessary? (b) Describe the structure and functioning of a nephron in human kidneys.
worked_examples.given: Cardiovascular double loop and renal filtration units.
worked_examples.formula: Double circulation: Pulmonary circuit (heart -> lungs -> heart) + Systemic circuit (heart -> body -> heart).
worked_examples.substitution: Trace blood flow and ultrafiltration in nephron.
worked_examples.calculation:
(a) Double circulation: Blood flows through the four-chambered heart twice during one complete cycle through the body (pulmonary circulation to oxygenate blood, systemic circulation to supply tissues). Necessity: Completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, ensuring high oxygen delivery efficiency to maintain constant homeostatic body temperature (endothermy).
(b) Nephron Function: 1. Ultrafiltration: High hydrostatic pressure in glomerulus forces water, glucose, amino acids, salts, and urea into Bowman's capsule forming glomerular filtrate. 2. Selective Reabsorption: Along proximal tubule and loop of Henle, useful substances (glucose, ions, water) are reabsorbed into peritubular capillaries. 3. Tubular Secretion: Extra ions and urea are secreted into collecting duct to form urine.
worked_examples.finalAnswer: (a) Double circulation passes blood twice through the heart, ensuring complete separation of oxygenated/deoxygenated blood; (b) Nephron filters blood in glomerulus, reabsorbs nutrients in tubules, and collects urine.
